title: RBAC permission denied error states + copy patterns (Console)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
## Context
RBAC v2 introduces deny-by-default authorization enforcement across Gateway + Control Plane + Console. For regulated enterprise workloads, we need consistent, evidence-friendly, and user-helpful “permission denied” error states.

Today the Console has inconsistent patterns:
- Generic “Something went wrong” toasts for 403s
- Missing admin guidance (who can fix it / what to request)
- No consistent language for “not allowed” vs “not authenticated”
- No escalation path for Private/Dedicated operators (where support may route differently)

This ticket defines **Console error states + copy patterns** for permission denied across primary workflows, including admin guidance and escalation links. Align with engineering work on **denial reason codes** and optional **debug headers** to support “why was I denied?” without leaking sensitive policy details.

Related work/artifacts:
- Confluence spec (role management UX): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-role-management-ux.json
- API semantics/patterns: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/authorization-check-patterns.json
- Denial reason codes PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-28241-add-denial-reason-codes-and-debug-header.json
- Permission naming/versioning ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-014-permission-naming-and-versioning.json

## Goals
1) Define a consistent taxonomy of denial states for the Console (401 vs 403 vs “needs scope”).
2) Provide copy that is:
   - Clear and non-accusatory
   - Helpful for end users and admins
   - Safe (doesn’t expose sensitive internal policy details)
   - Easy to localize later (short, modular strings)
3) Provide escalation paths:
   - “Contact your Org Admin / Security Admin” guidance
   - Link to “RBAC & Permissions” docs page (public docs) when available
   - Link to Support for Dedicated/Private customers (where applicable)
4) Define UI presentation patterns across: page-level blocks, inline form errors, modals, and toasts.

## Non-goals
- Building the actual UI components (handled in Console implementation tickets).
- Designing a full policy explanation UI (covered by role management UI specs; this ticket only defines the error/empty states and copy).
- Exposing exact permission strings to non-admin users by default (permission viewer exists for admins; default denied messaging should be more general).

## Principles
- **Default to minimal detail.** Provide more detail only when the viewer is an org admin/security admin OR when an “admin debug mode” is explicitly enabled.
- **Never suggest that the user did something wrong.** Frame as “You don’t have access” not “You are not allowed.”
- **Actionable next step always present** (request access, switch org/project, contact support).
- **Consistent terminology:** Use “permission” (not “role”) in denied messages; role is a possible fix.
- **Avoid disclosing resource existence.** For some resources, the safer response is “Not found or no access” (see taxonomy).

---

## Taxonomy: auth-related error states
This is the mapping the Console should use when rendering errors from API/Gateway.

### A) Not signed in / session expired (HTTP 401)
**When:** Missing/expired session, invalid token, SSO refresh required.
**UI:** Blocking page-level state if critical, otherwise modal/toast with sign-in CTA.
**Primary CTA:** “Sign in” / “Re-authenticate”
**Secondary CTA:** “Go to status page” only if relevant.

Copy:
- Title: “Sign in required”
- Body: “Your session has expired or you’re signed out. Sign in to continue.”

### B) Permission denied (HTTP 403)
**When:** Authenticated but policy evaluation denies the action.
**UI:** Depends on context (see patterns below). Always include “Request access” guidance.

Copy (base):
- Title: “You don’t have permission to do this”
- Body (default): “Ask an organization admin to grant access, or switch to an account with the required permissions.”

Optional detail (admin-only / debug):
- “Required permission: <permission>”
- “Scope: <org/project/environment>”
- “Reason: <reason code friendly name>”

### C) Resource not found vs no access (HTTP 404/403 depending on endpoint)
Some endpoints will intentionally return 404 to avoid leaking existence. Console should not over-assume.

Copy:
- Title: “We can’t find this resource”
- Body: “It may have been deleted, you may not have access, or the link may be incorrect.”
- CTA: “Back to <list page>”
- Admin hint (small text, admin-only): “If you believe you should have access, check your role bindings or contact your admin.”

### D) Wrong scope / needs different project/environment
**When:** The user is allowed in org, but not in selected project/environment; or action is scoped and requires different selection.
**UI:** Inline guidance where scope picker exists.

Copy:
- Title: “Access is limited to specific scope”
- Body: “Switch to a project/environment where you have access, or request access for this scope.”
- CTA: “Switch scope” (opens scope selector)

### E) Break-glass / elevated access required (rare)
We should not encourage break-glass casually.

Copy (shown only when policy returns explicit code for it, e.g., `BREAK_GLASS_REQUIRED`):
- Title: “Admin approval required”
- Body: “This action requires time-bound elevated access. Contact your Security Admin.”

### F) Feature not enabled / license restriction (HTTP 402/403 with entitlement code)
Not strictly “permission denied,” but frequently confusable.

Copy:
- Title: “Not available on your plan”
- Body: “This feature isn’t enabled for your deployment. Contact Support to enable it.”
- CTA: “Contact Support” (Dedicated/Private) / “View plans” (Hosted)

---

## UI patterns (where and how to show)

### 1) Page-level blocking state (primary pattern)
**Use when:** User navigates to a page dedicated to an action they cannot perform (e.g., Role Management page, Audit Log Export page).

Layout:
- Icon/illustration (standard Console empty state)
- Title + body
- Primary CTA: “Back” or “Go to overview”
- Secondary CTA: “Request access” (opens instructions modal) or “Copy request details”

Copy (403):
- Title: “You don’t have access to this page”
- Body: “Ask an organization admin to grant the required permissions. If you think this is a mistake, contact Support.”

Request access helper (inline or modal):
- “Send this request to your admin:”
- Include prefilled text block the user can copy:
  - “Please grant me access to <page/action> in <org> (<project/env if applicable>). My user: <email>.”

### 2) Inline disabled controls + tooltip (preventive pattern)
**Use when:** We can reliably know permissions ahead of time (e.g., permission viewer in role mgmt pages, scoped capabilities returned from API).

Behavior:
- Disable button with tooltip: “You don’t have permission to <verb>.”
- Tooltip secondary line (admin-only): “Requires <permission>.”

Copy:
- Tooltip: “You don’t have permission to edit routing policies.”
- Tooltip (admin-only): “Requires `routingPolicy.update` in this environment.”

### 3) Inline error on form submit (optimistic UI)
**Use when:** User attempts action and receives 403.

Behavior:
- Keep modal open (do not dismiss)
- Show error banner at top of modal
- Keep primary action disabled only if retry is useless; otherwise allow retry

Copy (banner):
- “Permission denied. You don’t have access to complete this action.”
- Link: “Learn how to request access”

### 4) Toast/snackbar (non-blocking)
**Use when:** Minor action fails due to permission (e.g., copying a secret value, exporting a small report) but user can continue elsewhere.

Copy:
- “Permission denied. Ask an admin for access.”
- Action: “Details” (opens small modal with request-access instructions)

### 5) “Why was I denied?” details (admin-only)
**Use when:** Viewer has admin-like permission OR a debug header is present OR a “Show technical details” toggle is enabled.

Contents:
- Decision: “Denied”
- Action: “<friendly action name>” (e.g., “Export audit logs”)
- Required permission: `<permission>`
- Scope: `<org>/<project>/<environment>`
- Reason code: `<code>` (mapped to friendly text)
- Request ID: `<request_id>`

Important: The default user view should **not** show permission strings or internal codes.

---

## Denial reason codes → user-visible copy mapping
Engineering is adding structured reason codes. Below are recommended friendly mappings.

- `MISSING_PERMISSION`
  - User: “Your account doesn’t have the required permission.”
  - Admin: “Missing permission: `<permission>`.”

- `SCOPE_MISMATCH`
  - User: “You don’t have access in the selected scope.”
  - Admin: “Denied for scope `<scope>`; check role bindings for this project/environment.”

- `ROLE_BINDING_NOT_FOUND`
  - User: “You don’t currently have access. Ask an admin to grant access.”
  - Admin: “No role binding found for subject in this scope.”

- `POLICY_VERSION_UNAVAILABLE` (rare; should be treated as error)
  - User: “We couldn’t verify access due to a temporary issue. Try again.”
  - Admin: Include request ID; suggest contacting Support if persistent.

- `BREAK_GLASS_REQUIRED`
  - User: “Admin approval required for this action.”
  - Admin: “Requires break-glass elevation. Follow internal procedure.”

- `ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED`
  - User: “This feature isn’t enabled for your deployment.”
  - Admin: “Entitlement missing: `<entitlement>`.”

---

## Escalation links and routing
We need consistent places to send users.

### Hosted
- “Contact Support” links to: https://console.redwoodinference.com/support (or intercom entry point)
- “RBAC & permissions” docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/security/rbac (placeholder; docs PR will confirm)

### Dedicated / Private
- If Support link is allowed, route to the account-specific support channel.
- Private (air-gapped) may not have direct link-out; show “Contact your deployment operator” instead, with configurable admin contact text (set by org admin).

Recommended UI logic:
- If deployment = Private and `support_link` is not configured, show:
  - “Contact your deployment operator or Security Admin.”
- If `support_link` configured, show:
  - Secondary CTA: “Contact Support”

---

## Specific Console surfaces (minimum coverage)
1) Role management pages (list, create, edit, assign)
2) API keys page (create/rotate/revoke)
3) Audit logs export/download
4) Routing policy edit flows (Dedicated + Private)
5) Private deployment settings (cluster operations, installer/admin bootstrap pages)

For each surface, use:
- Page-level blocking state for navigation to restricted page
- Inline banner for action-level 403s within modals

---

## Accessibility + content guidelines
- Use plain language; avoid jargon (RBAC, bindings) unless behind “technical details.”
- Ensure error states are keyboard navigable; focus should move to the error banner.
- Ensure color contrast for warning banners; do not rely on color alone.
- Provide a copy-to-clipboard control for “request access” text.

---

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Defined copy for 401 vs 403 vs not-found-or-no-access.
- [x] Defined page-level, modal/banner, tooltip, and toast patterns.
- [x] Included escalation paths for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private.
- [x] Mapped denial reason codes to friendly strings, with guidance on admin-only details.
- [x] Reviewed with PM + Console Eng for feasibility and safety.

## Open questions
1) Do we want to standardize “organization admin” vs “org admin” in all UI? (Recommendation: “organization admin” in body text, “Org Admin” only in role names.)
2) Should we ever show “Required permission” to non-admin users? (Recommendation: no; show only in admin debug/details.)
3) For 404/403 ambiguity, do we want a single shared copy block across the Console? (Recommendation: yes; consistent “may be deleted or you may not have access.”)

## Handoff notes for engineering
- Prefer an `AuthzErrorState` component with variants: `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `notFoundOrNoAccess`, `scopeMismatch`, `entitlement`.
- The component should accept optional fields:
  - `requestId`
  - `reasonCode`
  - `requiredPermission`
  - `scope`
  - `supportLink`
- Render “technical details” only when `viewerIsAdmin === true` OR `x-rw-authz-debug` is enabled.
